keywords.def: wear clothes with bright colours, large patterns and bold designs
artwork designed to create an interactive experience in a specific space
happening differently from what you would expect

sentences.en: Hello.
sentences.zh: 你好。

sentences.en: This is 6 Minute English from BBC Learning English.
sentences.zh: 这里是BBC学英语的6分钟英语节目。

sentences.en: I'm Neil. And I'm Georgie. Neil, I'm going to play you two sound recordings, and I want you to tell me how you feel when you hear them.
sentences.zh: 我是Neil。我是Georgie。Neil，我要放给你两段录音，我想让你告诉我听完后有什么感觉。

sentences.en: OK. First this…
sentences.zh: 好的。先听这个……

sentences.en: And now this.
sentences.zh: 现在是这个。

sentences.en: Oh, well, that first clip made me feel really relaxed.
sentences.zh: 哦，第一段音频让我感觉真的很放松。

sentences.en: But the second one – oh, it's horrible! I felt quite stressed out actually.
sentences.zh: 但第二段——哦，太可怕了！其实我感到压力挺大的。

sentences.en: Oh no! Well, this little experiment shows how much we are affected by the noise around us.
sentences.zh: 哦，不！嗯，这个小实验表明我们受周围噪音的影响有多大。

sentences.en: And that's a problem if you're one of the four billion people around the world who live in cities.
sentences.zh: 如果你是全世界生活在城市的四十亿人口之一，这就是个问题。

sentences.en: Yes, whether it's the rattle of train tracks, honking car horns, or the roar of aeroplanes overhead, modern cities are full of noise and this can have serious effects.
sentences.zh: 是的，无论是铁轨的咣当声、汽车的按喇叭声，还是头顶飞机轰鸣声，现代城市都充满了噪音，这会产生严重的影响。

sentences.en: The World Health Organisation reports that by 2050, around 2.5 billion people will experience hearing loss, and exposure to loud noise has been linked to stress and anxiety.
sentences.zh: 世界卫生组织报告称，到2050年，约有25亿人将面临听力损失，而暴露于噪音之中与压力和焦虑有关。

sentences.en: In this episode, we'll be hearing about ways to make our cities quieter, more relaxing places, using some useful new words and phrases.
sentences.zh: 在本期节目中，我们将听到如何让城市变得更安静、更放松的地方，并学习一些有用的新词汇和短语。

sentences.en: And remember, you'll find all the vocabulary along with a quiz and worksheet on our website, bbclearningenglish.com.
sentences.zh: 请记住，你可以在我们的网站 bbclearningenglish.com 上找到所有的词汇以及测验和练习页。

sentences.en: But now I have a question for you, Georgie.
sentences.zh: 但现在我有一个问题要问你，Georgie。

sentences.en: Sound is measured in units called decibels.
sentences.zh: 声音是用被称为分贝的单位来衡量的。

sentences.en: But how many decibels would it be if I whispered?
sentences.zh: 但如果我耳语，会有多少分贝呢？

sentences.en: A whisper is speaking like this. Is it: a) 3 decibels, b) 13 decibels, or c) 30 decibels?
sentences.zh: 耳语就像这样说话。是：a) 3分贝，b) 13分贝，还是 c) 30分贝？

sentences.en: Oh, that's really hard. I'll go for b) 13 decibels.
sentences.zh: 哦，这太难了。我选 b) 13分贝。

sentences.en: Well, we'll find out the answer at the end of the programme.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我们将在节目结束时揭晓答案。

sentences.en: Let's start in one of the noisiest cities in the world – Mumbai in India, where daytime noise levels regularly hit 80 decibels, which is over 20 decibels higher than World Health Organisation recommendations.
sentences.zh: 让我们从世界上噪声最大的城市之一——印度孟买开始，在那里的日间噪声水平经常达到80分贝，这比世界卫生组织的建议值高出20多分贝。

sentences.en: Listen to Mumbai native Chhavi Sachdev share her experiences of living in this noisy city with BBC World Service programme People Fixing the World.
sentences.zh: 听听孟买本地人Chhavi Sachdev与BBC世界频道节目《拯救世界的人们》分享她在喧闹城市生活的经历。

sentences.en: I mean, India in general is just really loud.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，印度整体来说就是真的很吵。

sentences.en: We are a loud people. We dress loud, we talk loud, we celebrate loud, we watch movies loud.
sentences.zh: 我们是一个喧闹的民族。我们穿得很显眼，我们说话声音大，我们庆祝得很热闹，我们看电影声音也很大。

sentences.en: When people ask me what I miss about living abroad, I tell them it's the quiet, because after 12 years of living in the US and Europe, when I got back, I realised I couldn't handle it anymore.
sentences.zh: 当人们问我怀念在国外生活的什么时，我告诉他们是安静，因为在美國和欧洲生活了12年之后，当我回到这里时，我意识到我再也受不了了。

sentences.en: I'd gotten used to lower levels of noise.
sentences.zh: 我已经习惯了较低的噪声水平。

sentences.en: Chhavi says, "Indians talk loud, celebrate loud and dress loud." To dress loud means to wear clothes with bright colours and large, bold patterns.
sentences.zh: Chhavi说，“印度人说话声音大，庆祝时热闹，穿着也显眼。”穿得显眼（dress loud）是指穿色彩鲜艳、图案大而醒目的衣服。

sentences.en: When Chhavi returned to India after living overseas, she says she couldn't handle the noise.
sentences.zh: 当Chhavi在海外生活后回到印度时，她说她无法忍受这种噪音。

sentences.en: If you can't handle something, you find it difficult to deal or cope with.
sentences.zh: 如果你无法应对（can't handle）某事，你会发现很难处理或应付它。

sentences.en: So, what can be done to tackle noise in cities like Mumbai?
sentences.zh: 那么，可以采取什么措施来解决像孟买这样的城市的噪音问题呢？

sentences.en: One interesting approach involves using sound itself to make things feel quieter.
sentences.zh: 一种有趣的方法是利用声音本身来让人感觉更安静。

sentences.en: Soundscaping is the idea of adding certain sounds to busy public spaces so that they sound and feel more relaxing.
sentences.zh: 声景（Soundscaping）是在繁忙的公共场所添加某些声音的理念，使它们听起来和感觉起来更放松。

sentences.en: Sound artist Charles Montambault lives near the Parc des Madelinots, a busy city park in Montreal, Canada.
sentences.zh: 声音艺术家Charles Montambault住在加拿大蒙特利尔一个繁忙的城市公园——马德利诺公园附近。

sentences.en: Charles was inspired to recreate the ocean sounds he heard on holiday in the Magdalen Islands in his city park back home.
sentences.zh: Charles受到他在马格德林群岛度假时听到的海洋声音的启发，在他家乡的城市公园里重新创作了这些声音。

sentences.en: On BBC World Service programme People Fixing the World, he tells reporter Natasha Fernandes that these sounds included ocean waves and some unusual-sounding sand.
sentences.zh: 在BBC世界服务节目《拯救世界的人们》中，他告诉记者Natasha Fernandes，这些声音包括海浪和一些听起来不寻常的沙子。

sentences.en: The sand on the Magdalen Islands can sing.
sentences.zh: 马格德林群岛的沙子会唱歌。

sentences.en: When you walk into the sand firmly, the sand makes some squeaky sounds, so that's one sound that is kind of funny, kind of special.
sentences.zh: 当你用力踩进沙子里时，沙子会发出吱吱的声音，所以这是一种有点搞笑、有点特别的声音。

sentences.en: Inside the small park, surrounded by busy roads, Charles and his team set up an immersive sound art installation in the form of speakers planted in flower beds.
sentences.zh: 在这个被繁忙道路环绕的小公园里，Charles和他的团队设置了一个沉浸式的声音艺术装置，形式是种植在花坛里的扬声器。

sentences.en: So, the art installation was really to make this park a little quieter by adding some quiet noises.
sentences.zh: 所以，这个艺术装置真的是通过增加一些安静的声音来让这个公园变得更安静一点。

sentences.en: So, it's counterintuitive, but you can make a park less noisy by adding some calmer sounds.
sentences.zh: 所以，这违反直觉，但你可以通过添加一些更平静的声音来让公园不那么吵。

sentences.en: The sand on the Magdalen Islands is squeaky – it makes a high-pitched sound called a squeak when stepped on.
sentences.zh: 马格德林群岛的沙子是会发出吱吱声的——踩上去时会发出一种叫作吱吱声（squeak）的高音。

sentences.en: Charles played recordings of this sand, ocean waves and other relaxing sounds through speakers hidden in the park.
sentences.zh: Charles通过藏在公园里的扬声器播放了这种沙子、海浪和其他放松声音的录音。

sentences.en: He created an art installation – a work of art designed to give people an interactive experience.
sentences.zh: 他创作了一个艺术装置——一件旨在给人互动体验的艺术品。

sentences.en: By adding more relaxing sounds, Charles' art installation actually made the park feel quieter.
sentences.zh: 通过添加更多放松的声音，Charles的艺术装置实际上让公园感觉更安静了。

sentences.en: It's an example of something that's counterintuitive, meaning it happens differently from how you would expect.
sentences.zh: 这是一个违背直觉（counterintuitive）的例子，意思是它的发生方式与你的预期不同。

sentences.en: What a great idea! And similar soundscapes are now helping city dwellers relax in other cities too, including Tokyo and Barcelona.
sentences.zh: 多么棒的主意啊！类似的声景现在也在包括东京和巴塞罗那在内的其他城市帮助城市居民放松。

sentences.en: Now Neil, you asked me a question about a very quiet sound – a whisper.
sentences.zh: 现在Neil，你问了我一个关于非常安静的声音——耳语的问题。

sentences.en: So, are you going to reveal the correct answer?
sentences.zh: 那么，你要揭晓正确答案了吗？

sentences.en: I asked you how loud a whisper is. Yes, and I said 13 decibels.
sentences.zh: 我问你耳语有多大声。是的，我说的是13分贝。

sentences.en: Well, 13 is an unlucky number and you are wrong.
sentences.zh: 嗯，13是个不吉利的数字，你猜错了。

sentences.en: Ah! It was actually 30. OK. Let's recap the vocabulary we've learned, starting with decibel – the unit for measuring sound.
sentences.zh: 啊！其实是30。好的。让我们回顾一下我们学过的词汇，从分贝（decibel）开始——这是测量声音的单位。

sentences.en: Someone who dresses loud likes to wear clothes with bright colours and bold designs.
sentences.zh: 穿得很显眼（dresses loud）的人喜欢穿颜色鲜艳、设计大胆的衣服。

sentences.en: If you can't handle something, you find it difficult to deal with.
sentences.zh: 如果你无法应付（can't handle）某事，你会发现很难处理它。

sentences.en: An art installation is an artwork designed to create an interactive experience in a certain space.
sentences.zh: 艺术装置（art installation）是一种旨在特定空间中创造互动体验的艺术品。

sentences.en: The adjective squeaky describes things which make a high-pitched sound like a mouse.
sentences.zh: 形容词“吱吱叫的”（squeaky）形容发出像老鼠一样高音的事物。

sentences.en: Squeak, squeak! And finally, if you call something counterintuitive, you mean it happens differently from how you would expect.
sentences.zh: 吱吱，吱吱！最后，如果你称某事为违背直觉的（counterintuitive），你的意思是它的发生方式与你的预期不同。

sentences.en: Once again, our six minutes are up, but if you'd like to hear more about this and many other trending topics, you'll find more episodes and learning activities on our website, bbclearningenglish.com.
sentences.zh: 我们的六分钟又到了，但如果你想听到更多关于这个和许多其他热门话题的内容，你可以在我们的网站 bbclearningenglish.com 上找到更多节目和学习活动。

sentences.en: See you again soon. But for now, it's goodbye.
sentences.zh: 很快再见。但现在，我们要说再见了。

sentences.en: Goodbye...!
sentences.zh: 再见……!
